name: Eswatini Slaai
description: Slaai, a distinctively Swazi avocado salad, is genuinely unlike a typical avocado salad found elsewhere - real technique combines avocado with coconut, ginger, and crushed peanuts together, a real, specific combination unique to Eswatini, not just avocado with a generic vinaigrette.

ingredients_full.ingredient: Peanuts, all types, dry-roasted, with salt

ingredients.ingredient: Peanuts, all types, dry-roasted, with salt

steps_detailed: Mix the lemon juice, ginger, and salt together.
Add the avocado and toss gently to coat, then marinate at room temperature 20 minutes.
Drizzle with the coconut milk and scatter the crushed peanuts over the top just before serving.

name: Eswatini Sishwala
description: Sishwala, a thick maize porridge, is Eswatini's most essential staple, similar to South African pap - real technique adding the maize meal gradually while stirring constantly builds its dense, smooth texture.
steps_detailed: Whisk about a third of the cornmeal with the salt into 1.25 cups boiling water.
Gradually beat in the remaining cornmeal, stirring constantly, over medium-low heat 15-18 minutes, until very thick and smooth.
steps: Whisk about a third of the cornmeal with the salt into 1.25 cups boiling water.

name: Eswatini Umbidvo Wetintsanga
description: Umbidvo wetintsanga, pumpkin leaves cooked with real ground peanuts, is a beloved Swazi dish - real pumpkin leaves aren't a distinct item here, so spinach stands in for a milder approximation.

ingredients_full.ingredient: Peanuts, all types, dry-roasted, with salt

ingredients.ingredient: Peanuts, all types, dry-roasted, with salt

steps_detailed: Cook the onion 3-4 minutes.
Add the spinach and a splash of water, and simmer 12-15 minutes.
Stir in the ground peanuts and simmer 5-6 minutes more.

name: Eswatini Setindlubu Siphuphe
description: Setindlubu siphuphe, a thick porridge made from real ground peanut puree, is a genuine Swazi specialty, real technique simmering the ground peanuts slowly until the mixture thickens naturally.

ingredients_full.ingredient: Peanuts, all types, dry-roasted, with salt

ingredients.ingredient: Peanuts, all types, dry-roasted, with salt

steps_detailed: Whisk the ground peanuts with the milk and 0.5 cup water into a smooth mixture.
Simmer gently, stirring often, 15-18 minutes, until it thickens into a smooth, spoonable porridge.

name: Eswatini Smoked Beef
description: Smoked beef, marinated with spices before real smoking, is a beloved Swazi specialty, real technique letting the marinade penetrate before the smoke does its work.
steps_detailed: Rub the beef with the garlic, paprika, and pepper, and marinate at least 30 minutes.
Grill or smoke over indirect heat, turning occasionally, 20-25 minutes, until cooked through with a real smoky char.

name: Eswatini Corn Bread (Sinkhwa Sembila)
description: Sinkhwa sembila, a steamed corn bread, is a genuine Swazi specialty, real technique steaming rather than baking, giving it a soft, moist, pudding-like texture.
steps_detailed: Blend the corn kernels roughly, then mix with the flour, milk, egg, sugar, and melted butter into a thick batter.
Pour into a small greased dish and steam over simmering water 35-40 minutes until set.

description: Roasted corn on the cob is a beloved Swazi snack, real technique roasting directly over the flame until charred in spots.
steps_detailed: Grill or roast the corn directly over an open flame, turning occasionally, 10-12 minutes, until charred in spots and tender.

name: Eswatini Pumpkin Porridge
description: Sidvudvu, pumpkin porridge mixed with cornmeal, is a genuine Swazi comfort food, real technique cooking the pumpkin down until it breaks apart into the porridge.
steps_detailed: Simmer the squash in 1.5 cups water 15-18 minutes until it breaks down completely.
Whisk in the cornmeal, stirring constantly, and simmer 10-12 minutes more until thick.

Add the tomatoes and simmer 12-15 minutes until thickened.
